---
title: "The rules"
---

Three rules, in order. The first that decides wins, and its name is returned with the
gender.

| Rule | Decides when | Gender |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dottir` | the last name ends in *-dóttir* | female |
| `given_name` | a given name is registered only as a boy's or only as a girl's name | that name's |
| `son` | the last name ends in *-son* | male |

Anything else is unknown: `gender` is `None` in Python, empty in a CSV.

## 1. `dottir`

The last name ends in *-dóttir*. A patronymic or matronymic ending in *-dóttir* is only ever
a woman's, so nothing else is consulted.

```
Helga Ingimundardóttir   →  female  dottir
```

## 2. `given_name`

The first given name the register lists only as a boy's name (*drengjanafn*) or only as a
girl's name (*stúlknanafn*).

- **Given names** are every name but the last. A single name is its own given name.
- **Unisex names** — registered for both boys and girls — are passed over, as are names the
  register lists only as middle names (*millinöfn*), and names it does not list at all.
- **Hyphenated names** are looked up whole and then part by part: *Anna-Lísa* is found
  through *Anna* even if the pair is not registered.

```
Ingimundur Helgason      →  male    given_name (Ingimundur)
```

## 3. `son`

The last name ends in *-son*. This is checked only after the given names, because *-son* is
also a family name: *Helga Ingimundarson* is a woman, and her given name says so first.

```
Helga Ingimundarson      →  female  given_name (Helga)
```

Without the order, a woman with a *-son* family name would be counted as a man. That was the
bug in the surname-first rule this package replaced.

## Normalizing the input

Names are split on whitespace and commas, and stray dots are dropped, so
`"Ingimundardóttir, Helga"` and `"Helga  Ingimundardóttir"` both split into two parts.

::: {.callout-warning}
## A "Last, First" name is not reordered

The last part is always taken as the last name. `"Ingimundardóttir, Helga"` is read as given
name *Ingimundardóttir* and last name *Helga*, and comes out unknown. Put names in natural
order before classifying them.
:::

Register lookups are case-insensitive but accent-sensitive: *Guðmundur* is in the register,
*Gudmundur* is not. Names transliterated to ASCII will often come out unknown.
